name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Implement a centralized platform for sharing project updates across departments, managed by the project management team. This will improve transparency and collaboration, allowing teams to stay informed about progress and challenges in real-time. The trade-off is the initial time investment to set up and train staff on the new system, but the long-term benefits in efficiency and reduced miscommunication far outweigh this cost.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s centralized platform risks becoming another silo if it’s just a passive broadcast tool. Instead, force a two-way contract: every update must include a clear next decision or action, owned by a named person. That turns transparency into accountability. Settle it by piloting this with one high-stakes project and measuring whether it reduces unresolved blockers by 20% in 30 days.

name: Chisel
text:
**Decision:** Require every cross-department project to start with a one-page "decision log" that lists the first three choices the team must make, the person accountable for each, and the deadline for each choice.

This forces clarity upfront and prevents projects from drifting while waiting for consensus. The trade-off is slower starts for some teams, but it saves weeks of back-and-forth later.
[dispatched 3 workers: worker-3800, worker-9709, worker-7847 — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s one-page "decision log" risks becoming a static artifact that teams game to check a box, not a living tool. The real risk is that tying it to exec syncs turns it into a compliance exercise—teams fill it out to avoid scrutiny, not to drive action. Settle it by piloting it with a single high-stakes project and measuring whether it actually accelerates decisions, not just documentation.
